Pittsburgh:
The day after Christmas, 2011. I had just spent seven months in Fairfield, Iowa, and I was quite tired of small-town life, so I took a Greyhound from Columbus to New York. I had read about a murder on a Greyhound bus, but I like a bit of adventure, and I wanted to see the country go by instead of flying over it.

From Columbus it was mostly farmland, and after dark there was almost nothing: dark, empty country, with only a few scattered lights coming from somewhere out in the wild. Then the bus drove into a tunnel that felt like it would never end. When we came out the other side, the city was suddenly there, all lit up, bright and beautiful. It was Christmas week, so maybe it was dressed up even more than usual.

The bus raced along the river, and I pressed against the window, staring at the lights on the other side. This is what a city is supposed to look like, I thought. Fairfield was tiny, and even Columbus didn't feel big enough.

The bus stopped for about half an hour. I wandered down the street to the river and took one more long look at the other side before getting back on.
